name: Pixel art / 8-bit game world
look: chunky integer-scaled pixels, 16 to 32 colours, sprites on 2s, parallax by whole pixels, dither; the product lives inside a game level.

products: anything with levels, quests or unlocks
fits.notes: dev tools, games, creative tools, nostalgia, playful B2C, "unlocks/levels/quests" metaphors

when_not: Avoid for finance trust, healthcare, luxury; avoid if the film needs to look like the real app throughout (use pixel only as a layer, e.

type.guidance: Press Start 2P, Silkscreen, Pixelify Sans, or m5x7 for UI
type.rule: Style type is for the world's chrome and display; the brand face always sets the real claim line and any product UI text.

colour.guidance: Press Start 2P, Silkscreen, Pixelify Sans, or m5x7 for UI; pair with a clean grotesk for the real claim. 8-colour palettes (PICO-8, Sweetie-16, Game Boy 4-green); one signal colour for the product.
colour.rule: Style palette fills the world; the brand colour takes the role named in brand_lock.colour_role and never drops below the contrast of the brand's own palette.

keeps: real product UI capture (composited as a screen plate, never redrawn)
brand_lock.colour_role: brand colour becomes the single signal colour of the palette; the other 7-15 colours come from the game palette
brand_lock.type_role: pixel face for in-world UI and labels; brand face sets the real claim line in clean type
brand_lock.world_changes: the product lives inside a game level; the real UI is a screen plate inside it
brand_lock.rule: Under a brand lock the brand colour, type and logo stay; the style world (material, picture language, motion grammar, finish, sound) is what varies between looks. A branded launch shows 3 different style worlds.

hints: render a low-res canvas (320x180) and `image-rendering: pixelated` scale
palette-swap day-to-night as a story beat
"level clear" bar as a progress device
motion_grammar.note: grammars lists existing library/grammars ids; grammars_planned lists world grammars the engine plan adds (game-world, tabletop, os-desktop, type-only, editorial, collage, cinematic-world).

effects.role: snap any plate or DOM-snapshot to the game palette
optional light CRT on the finale

effects_note: rasan-fx passes (runtime/rasan-fx.js); order is the pass order. {brand_colour} / {second_ink} are filled from the brand or look palette.

codex_assets.prompt_template: 16-bit side-scroller {subject}, limited {palette_size}-colour palette, no anti-aliasing, flat evenly lit flat chroma-green (#00FF00) background, equal 4x4 grid, no text; sprite sheet 4x4 of one character in poses (idle, walk, carry, celebrate), same seed words as the tileset
codex_assets.r1_note: sprite sheets (A4), tilesets, a hero scene plate "16-bit side-scroller, limited palette, no anti-aliasing"; then snap to palette in canvas. Stills animate via A4 and A1 with integer steps.
codex_assets.rules: Flat, evenly lit plain background (chroma green or pure white) for clean cut-outs; one prompt family with the same seed words; generate at 2x and downscale; never ask Codex for readable UI text or logos (typeset them in HTML).

palette: chiptune (square/triangle), coin pick-ups, 8-bit blips synced to cuts
a bitcrushed bass drop. Procedural music in `rasan-music.js` can do square waves

build.recipe: `runtime/medium-pixel.js` + `medium-pixel-companion.js`, grammar `pixel-collage`, style `pixel.md`, `systems/vernacular/pixel-game-ui.md`. Offscreen canvas at low res, draw rects, GSAP drives `time`, quantise to whole px with `Math.round`. Palette via a lookup quantiser in a tiny fragment shader. Three.js voxel scenes (see #3) are the 3D cousin.

product_ui_rule: If the film shows RasanAI Studio, use the current dark sidebar UI with the Describe...Final dot stepper (docs/brand/studio-ui/), as a real capture composited INTO this style; never the retired light UI.
